steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: Glaciated upland landscapes are attractive for tourism, recreation and economic development because of their dramatic scenery, distinctive landforms and sense of wilderness. However, their fragile environments and limited accessibility create challenges.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Lake District receives approximately 18 million visitors per year, generating an estimated £1.4 billion for the local economy and supporting around 18,000 jobs. Tourism accounts for roughly 40% of the Lake District's economy.

steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: The multiple uses of glaciated uplands create conflicts between different interest groups. Tourists, farmers, conservationists, quarrying companies, foresters and local residents all want different things from the same landscape.

steps.title: Key Facts
steps.body: The Lake District National Park was established in 1951 and covers 2,362 km². It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017. It receives approximately 18 million visitors per year and has around 42,000 residents.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use the Lake District as your main case study - know specific facts (18 million visitors, £1.4 billion, 42,000 residents) Always consider BOTH sides of tourism (benefits and problems) Know specific management strategies: Fix the Fells, park and ride, Environmental Stewardship, Sandford Principle For conflict questions, identify specific groups and explain WHY they disagree Link management strategies to the conflicts they address Remember the National Park's dual purpose: conservation AND enjoyment
